Amazon Pickup Mix-Up 1/3/22I had two packages that were supposed to be shipped out to UPS, one of which was an Amazon return and the other of which would not go through. The package that did not go through contained photos I needed to get developed for a music festival I took pictures for. I owed the organizer images, as I was on the media team for the event. These were to be sent to Georgia. I called UPS to fix the issue with the latter package, and then the following day, someone came to pick up a package. I gave him the film in error, thinking UPS must have solved my issue, only to realize that he came for the Amazon return, not for the film.Calls 1/3/22Following this realization, I proceeded to call UPS, whose representative told me they could do nothing, and bounced me to Amazon, whose representative also told me they could do nothing. I asked her if they could leave something that would let the Amazon shipping center in Virginia (where it was headed) that when they got the package it should be returned to me. She said that Amazon had no such system and I would need to wait until the [package made it to the facility. I asked her if she could put me through to the facility in Virginia so I could tell them myself. She said she had no such ability. I asked if she could transfer me to someone who could contact them. She explained that there was no such person. I thanked her for her time and called UPS again. This time, UPS said they would issue an interception order to stop the package from arriving. I thanked the representative and concluded the call, feeling relieved.Calls 1/4/22The following day, I awoke to find a message from my Amazon app which stated that a refund was applied to my account for my return. Frustrated, I called Amazon again and spoke to someone about the issue. I explained the situation and asked if she could get the package sent back to me. She explained that she was sorry, but the person who spoke to me last gave me false information. There was, in fact, a system of tickets that could be created to notify a shipping facility of a package that should be returned to the sender upon arrival. She told me that since the package arrived at the facility that morning, it has likely been opened, inspected, and the contents thrown away without me being notified. I explained to her that this was a departure from what the other representative told me and that the pictures on the film were for a music festival and were irreplaceable She apologized and said she would file a ticket anyway, just in case, but that I should expect to not get my pictures back. Despite the package being there already (complete with a shipping label and tracking number to aid in its location), she said it would take up to 15 days for the facility to even view the ticket, meaning my package would likely be long gone. She sighed and stated that things "could have been very different" if the first Amazon representative gave me the correct information. I asked why the system takes 15 days when packages are delivered sometimes in less than 2 days. She did not have an answer to this question. Frustrated, I explained that what was originally a mixup due to my lapse of memory has become the imminent loss of irreplaceable photo work and film rolls which were valued at a combined $45. I asked who I should speak to to get compensation for this incident in the event that I never get my film rolls back. She said that there was no such department and that Amazon would not offer compensation because the rolls were no Amazon products. I thanked her for her time and concluded the call. Less than 10 minutes later, I called Amazon support again. I was determined to do everything I could to get my package back. The third representative told me some of the information the second representative gave me was incorrect. She explained that once the package is received by the facility, it is not opened immediately but is rather thrown in a pile with packages to be sorted. According to her, it could take the aforementioned 15 days to find the package and a whole month to return it to me if they succeeded in locating it. She too, however, stated that there was a chance I would never receive it, before doubling back and sending me an email that stated I would get a confirmation email when the package was found.AftermathI am beyond frustrated with Amazon Customer Service. In recent times, there have been numerous instances of account closures by e-commerce giant Amazon without any explanation or proper communication to the affected customers. These abrupt closures have left customers frustrated, confused, and feeling violated. A negative trend of unexplained account closures is observed, highlighting the negative impact on customers and questioning the ethical practices of a company that prides itself on customer-centricity. Many customers, like myself, have fallen victim to Amazon's sudden account closures. Without warning or prior notice, access to accounts that have been faithfully used for years is abruptly terminated. When attempting to log in, a message appears stating that the account has been closed, with an email notification supposedly sent. However, in numerous cases, customers claim to have never received any such email or any details on how to resolve the situation.Adding to the frustration, attempts to seek clarification from Amazon's customer support often go unanswered. It is only when customers create new accounts and reach out to support that they receive a response, albeit in a rude form. The response typically states that the account was closed for violating the terms of the Conditions of Use agreement. However, customers vehemently deny any wrongdoing and are left perplexed by the lack of specific reasons for their account closures.Account closures without proper explanation or justification raise severe concerns about customer rights. As loyal patrons who have spent years and significant amounts of money on the platform, customers have the right to transparency and fair treatment. The sudden termination of access to accounts, which may contain valuable digital assets such as e-books and audio files, feels like a betrayal of trust. The alarming trend of unexplained account closures by Amazon raises serious questions about the company's commitment to customer satisfaction and respect for customer rights.
